title: Reading exit codes
description:
Turn a child process's exit code into something a person or a supervisor can act on (lesson 1.03):

```cpp
bool crashed(std::uint32_t code);
std::string describeExit(std::uint32_t code);
```

- **crashed** is true for NTSTATUS error codes: those whose top two bits are both set (`0xC0000000` to `0xFFFFFFFF`).
- **describeExit** returns:

| Code | Text |
|---|---|
| 0 | `success` |
| 259 | `still running` |
| `0xC0000005` | `crashed: access violation` |
| `0xC00000FD` | `crashed: stack overflow` |
| `0xC0000409` | `crashed: stack buffer overrun or fail-fast` |
| `0xC0000374` | `crashed: heap corruption` |
| `0xC000013A` | `stopped with Ctrl+C` |
| any other crash code | `crashed: 0xC0001234` (8 uppercase hex digits) |
| `0xE06D7363` | `unhandled C++ exception` |
| anything else | `failed with code N` (in decimal) |
hints: Check the specific codes first, then the general "is it a crash code" rule, then fall back to the plain number.
